item.title: [New] Exchange Online Admin API v2.0 drops Exchange.ManageV2 and Exchange.ManageAsAppV2 on 1 December; apps must move to Exchange.AdminAPI.Manage / .ManageAsApp and get fresh admin consent
item.description:
Every automation and third-party tool that administers Exchange through the Admin API needs a new consent grant this month; a rushed tenant-wide consent on an app-only Exchange administration permission is exactly the grant an attacker hopes to slip through, and a missed one breaks the tool on 1 December.

Exchange Online · Inventory service principals holding Exchange.ManageV2 or Exchange.ManageAsAppV2, grant the replacement only to apps you still need, verify their Exchange RBAC role, test, then remove the old permission before 1 December; alert on consent to Exchange.AdminAPI.ManageAsApp in AuditLogs.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [New] Exchange Online Admin API MailboxFolderPermission returns User as an object (DisplayName, Name, PrimarySmtpAddress) instead of a string from early November
item.description:
Scripts that audit mailbox folder delegation (a classic BEC persistence check) may silently fail or mis-attribute users after the change; the new PrimarySmtpAddress removes display-name ambiguity.

Exchange Online · Find scripts and tools that read MailboxFolderPermission through the Admin API, switch them to the User object and key on PrimarySmtpAddress, and re-run your folder-permission audit after the change.
